cards.b: An action by an organism or part of an organism causing a change of position or place.
The chemical reactions in cells that break down nutrient molecules and release energy for metabolism. Energy is released, never 'made'.
The ability to detect and respond to changes in the internal or external environment.
A permanent increase in size and dry mass. 'Getting bigger' alone is not enough.
The processes that make more of the same kind of organism.
The removal of waste products of metabolism and substances in excess of requirements.
The taking in of materials for energy, growth and development.
Magnification = image size ÷ actual size. It has no units; write it as ×400, for example.

cards.f: Convert mm to µm, and µm to mm
cards.b: 1 mm = 1000 µm. mm → µm: × 1000. µm → mm: ÷ 1000. Use the same unit for both sizes before dividing.

cards.f: Which structures does a bacterial cell have?
cards.b: Cell wall (not cellulose), cell membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes, circular DNA and plasmids. No nucleus, mitochondria or chloroplasts.
Contains the genetic material (chromosomes / DNA) that controls the cell's activities.
Mitochondria: aerobic respiration (release energy). Ribosomes: protein synthesis.

cards.f: Plant cell structures not found in animal cells
cards.b: Cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts (some cells) and a large permanent vacuole with cell sap. Plant cells DO have mitochondria.
Cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism. Xylem is a tissue; the heart and the leaf are organs.

cards.f: How is a red blood cell adapted to carry oxygen?
cards.b: Contains haemoglobin; no nucleus (more room for haemoglobin); biconcave shape gives a large surface area.

short.q: State three structures found in a plant cell but not in an animal cell. [3]
short.model: A cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole containing cell sap.

short.q: A white blood cell is 12 µm across. In a diagram it is 36 mm across. Calculate the magnification. [2]
points: convert to the same units (36 mm = 36 000 µm)

short.q: A bacterium appears 24 mm long in an image with magnification ×12 000. Calculate its actual length in µm. [2]
points: actual size = image size ÷ magnification = 0.002 mm

short.q: State three differences between a bacterial cell and an animal cell. [3]
short.model: Bacteria have no nucleus (circular DNA instead), have a cell wall and plasmids, and have no mitochondria.
points: no nucleus / circular DNA, animal has a nucleus
bacterium has a cell wall, animal cell does not

short.q: A car moves and uses fuel. Explain why a car is not a living organism. [2]
short.model: A living organism shows all seven characteristics. A car does not grow, reproduce, respire in cells or respond like an organism does.
points: living things show all seven characteristics (MRS GREN)
car does not grow / reproduce / excrete / show sensitivity
